title: Scope-Adaptive Enforcement via Precondition Composition
summary: RDD adopts precondition composition as the scope-adaptive enforcement pattern. `tier1-phase-manifest.yaml` per-phase entries gain an optional `applicable_when` block listing conditions (initial primitives: `cycle_type_in`, `cycle_type_not_in`, `phase_not_skipped`, `parent_cycle_present`, `parent_cycle_absent`); when any condition is unmet, the hook skips the check with `onFail: CONTINUE` semantics and records the skip in the dispatch log. Existing manifest entries without `applicable_when` continue to fire unconditionally, so standard full-pipeline cycles are unaffected. Preconditions cannot skip the compound check (ADR-064) for dispatches that already fired.
workflow_point: tier1-phase-manifest.yaml per-phase entries, evaluated by the Stop hook before each check
mechanism: applicable_when precondition block with onFail: CONTINUE semantics

links.note: preconditions cannot skip the compound check (ADR-064) for dispatches that did fire — the compound check remains unconditional for any dispatch that produced a dispatch-log entry
generalizes ADR-072's Skipped phases field, itself already an instance of the precondition pattern, into a named applicable_when primitive (phase_not_skipped)
the precondition primitives (cycle_type_in, parent_cycle_present, etc.) read the same per-entry fields ADR-078's multi-cycle schema declares
ADR-079's in-progress-gate predicate is a relaxation that could later be expressed as a precondition under this ADR's framework, though it is not implemented as one here
provides the enforcement primitive (legacy single-cycle format detection) that lets the hook treat pre-ADR-072 cycles permissively until ADR-081's migration path brings them under the new schema
